================================================================================
              HIGH LEVEL SYSTEM DESIGN ARCHITECTURE: TINDER
================================================================================
Authors/Credits: Inspired by Rajneesh Verma, Avash Mitra, and Gaurav Sen 
                 (InterviewReady System Design Series)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. SYSTEM REQUIREMENTS & SCOPE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Prioritized Functional Requirements:
1. Store profile data: Name, Age, Location (latitude/longitude), Bio, and 
   up to 5 profile images per user.
2. Issue authentication token via API Gateway upon signup/login.
3. Recommend candidate profiles based on geographical location, age bounds, 
   gender preferences, and past right/left swipe actions.
4. Record mutual right-swipes as matches.
5. Provide real-time 1-on-1 chat messaging between matched users.

Out of Scope:
- Profile moderation / content flagging.
- Payment subscriptions (Tinder Gold/Platinum).
- Enforcing daily swipe limits.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. CAPACITY ESTIMATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Daily Active Users (DAU): 10,000,000 (10 Million)
- Profile Images per user: 5 photos (~2 MB each)
- Total Image Storage: 10M * 5 * 2 MB = 100 Terabytes (TB)
- Matches per day: 0.1% of active users = 1,000,000 matches daily (~1,000/sec peak)
- Concurrent Chat Sockets: ~2,000,000 persistent connection streams at peak.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. ARCHITECTURE COMPONENTS & FLOW
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
[Client App] --> [API Gateway] --> [Microservices] --> [Databases & Caches]

Components:
1. API Gateway:
   - Load balancing across service instances.
   - Authentication token validation (JWT/OAuth2).
   - Rate limiting and request routing.

2. Distributed File System (DFS) & CDN:
   - Stores 5 profile images per user in cloud object storage (S3/GCS).
   - Serves static media via CDN nodes close to the user for low latency.

3. Relational Database (User DB):
   - Stores user attributes (name, age, location coordinates, bio).
   - Sharded horizontally by geographical location.
   - Configured in Master-Slave architecture for read resilience.

4. Matcher Service & Match DB:
   - Evaluates right-swipe events.
   - Identifies mutual right-swipes and records matches in indexed tables.

5. Session Service & Redis Cache:
   - Tracks active user connection streams (UserID -> ConnectionID).
   - Uses Redis cache to bypass database lookups on every message.

6. XMPP Chat Cluster:
   - Enables real-time peer-to-peer 1-on-1 messaging over persistent sockets.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. KEY DESIGN TRADE-OFFS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Trade-off 1: Image Storage (Files in DFS vs. BLOB in Database)
- Database BLOB: Offers mutability, transaction guarantees, and indexing, BUT 
  these features are useless for static image files. Causes database bloat.
- DFS + CDN (CHOSEN): Cheap, fast, highly scalable, and optimized for global 
  edge caching.

Trade-off 2: Messaging Protocol (HTTP Polling vs. XMPP / WebSockets)
- HTTP Polling: Repeated polling wastes bandwidth, drains device battery, 
  and overloads servers.
- XMPP (CHOSEN): Peer-to-peer persistent socket protocol allows instantaneous 
  bidirectional message delivery without polling.

Trade-off 3: Match Details Storage (Client-side vs. Server-side)
- Client-side: Saves server disk, but data is lost on app reinstall and easily 
  tampered with.
- Server-side (CHOSEN): Acts as immutable single source of truth, secure and 
  durable.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. DATABASE SCHEMA DEFINITIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Table: users
  - user_id (VARCHAR 36, PRIMARY KEY)
  - name (VARCHAR 100)
  - age (INT)
  - gender (VARCHAR 20)
  - target_gender (VARCHAR 20)
  - latitude (DECIMAL 9,6)
  - longitude (DECIMAL 9,6)
  - bio (TEXT)
  - created_at (TIMESTAMP)
  INDEX: idx_user_location (latitude, longitude)

Table: matches
  - match_id (VARCHAR 36, PRIMARY KEY)
  - user_id_1 (VARCHAR 36)
  - user_id_2 (VARCHAR 36)
  - is_matched (BOOLEAN)
  - created_at (TIMESTAMP)
  UNIQUE CONSTRAINT: (user_id_1, user_id_2)

Table: user_sessions
  - connection_id (VARCHAR 64, PRIMARY KEY)
  - user_id (VARCHAR 36)
  - server_node_ip (VARCHAR 45)
  - connected_at (TIMESTAMP)


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. API ENDPOINTS SPECIFICATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Profile Service:
  - POST /user/signup          -> Creates new account
  - GET  /user/login           -> Returns authentication token
  - GET  /user/:userID         -> Gets user profile
  - PUT  /user/:userID         -> Updates profile details/location
  - DELETE /user/:userID       -> Deletes user account

Session Service:
  - POST /session/connection/:userID1/:userID2 -> Links connection ID
  - GET  /session/users/:connectionID          -> Returns connected user pair
  - DELETE /session/connection/:connectionID    -> Removes session data

Matcher Service:
  - GET  /match                -> Returns all matches for logged-in user
  - POST /swipe                -> Records user swipe action
  - DELETE /match/:userID      -> Deletes user from match list

Recommendation Service:
  - GET  /recommendation       -> Returns ranked profile feed
